The Shattering of Oligoth

Ivar, The Uncrowned, The Bastard Prince, had fought Adrithyr to a standstill. The Battles were growing cumbersome and expensive to both the crown and the rebels. Ivar especially was suffering, his army was underfed, and spread far too thin to maintain the large area they had conquered. Adrithyr however, could not recognize his advantage. His advisors and generals, the best in all the realms, consisted of Lord Galahad, one of the greatest tacticians on the continent, The Red Wizard Kaela, a master of destruction and the arcane, and many more Knights and mages of great reputation. They continually urged him to make a real counter offensive effort, but he refused to take their advice. The Red King won his crown using tactics just like Ivar, in an albeit shorter and smaller scale rebellion, but still it was as if he had no idea how to stop an image of his former self. 

Ivar had made himself the de facto King west of the Warming River, calling his territory “The Uncrowned Kingdom”, which was a title beloved by those that believed Ivar had freed them of the evil King Adrithyr. One king was much like the other in the end, and taxes were raised to fund the war on both sides of the river. Kaela, keeping with her reputation as a sadist, said that Adrithyr should ride out on his griffon, alongside his Iron Knights and all the remaining 20 legions he had at his disposal, and meet Ivar at his capital city of Oligoth. It was a strong proposal, Oligoth was the home of house Mournraine, the family of Adrithyr’s queen Annabelle. This foothold Ivar had in Oligoth was an affront to the queen, he held a powerful fortress city along with the Queen’s blood within his grasp, and Adrithyr could not let that stand. 

Although he did oppose Ivar’s control of the city, he still would not advance his position enough, opting instead to send his son with 3 legions, fifteen hundred men. Fifteen hundred men against Ivar and his army of at least two thousand. Prince Lukas was no boy, he was young but in terms of sword skill and physical power, he was well beyond any knight in Estor, and even his own father. Some say the Prince should have turned his sword towards his father, and made peace with his lost bastard brother, but his loyalty was deeply rooted. Lukas was often seen as a slave to his father’s will, desperate to prove himself and fill the hole left in the King's heart by his wayward firstborn Kaladin.

Prince Lukas led his men from atop his wyvern, Tempest. A powerful beast combined with Lukas’ ability to control lightning, they were a force to be reckoned with. Unfortunately for the Prince, Ivar had harnessed the power of the Reckoner himself. The Prince’s army marched to the gates of Oligoth, where they met the forces of Ivar, a thousand men armed with crossbows and longbows. Lukas charged through the sky and called out to Ivar, challenging him in the name of their father, “Come out and show me who you are, Ivar! Let the sword decide who the true son of the King is!” Tempest shot a beam of electricity at the gates of the city, destroying the ancient stone towers and hard reinforced gate, opening the city to the invaders.

Ivar answered with chaos. The rogue never showed himself, or his true self, because charging out from the walls came a forty foot tall demon. The gray and red skin, curved and jagged black horns and the vile blade of Arkonil, the Betrayer God, led the armies of the rebel king out from the city. As the devil began to tear through the legions Lukas realized very quickly he could not stand against Ivar, he might be able to fight him for a time, but this battle was beyond his numbers. Lukas turned to flee, survival to fight tomorrow is better than never fighting again, a lesson taught to Lukas by one of his mentors and generals, Gullard Hothead. 

As Lukas turned his mount from the battle, Ivar pointed his sword up at the Prince and called out to him. The exact words are unknown, but the sentiment was that Ivar intended to do to the Queen (Lukas’ mother) what Adrithyr had done to Ivar’s mother. Without proper context of course this would seem quite a mundane threat, but with the history behind it, it's no wonder that Lukas charged head first toward the rebel, his heart filled with rage.

Ivar laughed in that great and terrible voice, like thunder, meeting with the sounds of actual thunder as Lukas gathered the storms around him. A great clash of demons blade and Princes thunder as the city came crashing down around them. The details are foggy from here, but the city was torn to pieces, towers broken and walls trampled by the might of the two sons of Adrithyr. Their battle was one for the ages, but in the end Ivar was too strong. The power of the Betrayer god and his martial prowess combined overwhelmed Lukas, and Ivar ripped him from the back of Tempest, and tore him in half at the waist. 

Oligoth was a ruin, no life remained within the walls, and barely half of Lukas’ army remained. They fled to tell the story, and Ivar left to tell his own. Prince Lukas was dead, and Oligoth was a gigantic crater of towers and walls, becoming known as “The Shattered Crown”.
